# Adversarial review: Epicenter file-editing API **Scope.** I couldn't use `read_thread` here, so this review is based only on the frozen snapshot. In that snapshot the nested proposal is already implemented. `packages/folder/src/edit-owner.ts:123-145` defines `BufferSnapshot` (`unread|loading|unavailable|ready`) with nested `Unsaved` (`dirty|saving|failed|conflict`), and the Svelte adapter, React adapter and all four apps already use it. I can't confirm anything the main conversation did after this snapshot. ## Verdict **FileEdit should be the buffer itself, with no container around it.** It should also not be one five-way status. The five candidate statuses cover three separate facts: 1. **Relationship:** whether the current text has landed in storage. 2. **Attempt:** whether a write is running, and which revision it carries. 3. **Source:** what we last learned about the stored file. Facts 1 and 2 overlap, but not completely. Fact 3 is fully independent. Your hypothesis holds, with one refinement: `failed` belongs to an attempt and should be dropped when the text changes, while `conflict` belongs to the base the text was edited from and should survive typing. That difference is what earns the union its place. **Callers back this up.** None of them treats `dirty` and `saving` differently: - Epicenter shows "Saving…" for both (`FileEditor.svelte:81`). - Capture does the same (`TextDetail.svelte:157-162`). - Whispering's `isSaving` merges them (`whispering.svelte.ts:1039-1041`). So a pending write is a flag inside "unsaved", not a sibling status. ## Definitions - **Base:** the exact stored content the held text was edited from, or the last revision that landed. - **Saved:** no held revision and no write running. "Saved" means the text equals the base as confirmed by the latest read or landed write. It does not mean the text matches storage right now. - **Unsaved:** a held revision exists that hasn't landed. Either the text differs from the base, or a write of other content is running. - **`save()`:** land the revision that is current when you call it. It resolves when that revision, or a later one that replaced it, has landed or failed. Typing after the call doesn't change what it resolves to. It returns the revision number it covered. - **Flush (internal only):** used by fences and close. It locks input, then saves until nothing is held or one attempt fails. Without the input lock, flush could chase typing forever, so it shouldn't be public. ## Proposed API ```ts type SaveState = | { status: 'saved' } | { status: 'unsaved'; saving: boolean } // saving may carry an older revision | { status: 'failed'; error: SaveFailure } // latest attempt of THIS text; nothing running | { status: 'conflict'; error: SaveConflict }; // base no longer matches storage; autosave paused type Stored = 'text' | 'missing' | 'not-text'; // last known, independent of SaveState type Editor = { readonly path: string; readonly text: string; // always present readonly markdown: Markdown; // same source, read with a schema readonly save: SaveState; readonly stored: Stored; readonly readError: ReadError | undefined; // latest refresh failed; older knowledge kept readonly locked: boolean; replaceText(text: string): ChangeResult; // refusals are returned, not stored change(c: DocumentChange): ChangeResult; save(): Promise>; revert(): Result; // returns the dropped text resolve(choice: 'theirs' | 'mine'): Promise>; refresh(): Promise>; subscribe(fn: () => void): () => void; [Symbol.dispose](): void; // ends this lease, never discards input }; folder.files.open(path, { signal }): Promise>; // missing | not-text | read failed ``` **Vanilla use:** ```ts const opened = await folder.files.open('notes/a.md'); if (opened.error) return show(opened.error); using editor = opened.data; editor.replaceText(editor.text + '\nmore'); const { data } = await editor.save(); // revision `data.revision` landed if (editor.save.status !== 'saved') /* newer typing is still held */; ``` **Svelte.** The adapter ties the lease to the component and makes the getters reactive: ```svelte {#await folder.files.open(path, { signal }) then opened} {#if opened.error}{:else}{/if} {:catch}…{/await}
{#if editor.locked}Another operation is using this file. {:else if editor.save.status === 'unsaved'}Saving… {:else if editor.save.status === 'failed'}Not saved: {editor.save.error.message} {:else if editor.save.status === 'conflict'}The saved file changed. {:else if editor.stored === 'missing'}Deleted elsewhere. Typing will ask before recreating it. {/if}
{#if editor.readError}

Couldn't check for changes: {editor.readError.message}

{/if}
